_README: Rope-capacity corrections for the 8 routes confirmed by the rule-3 triage.
A rope doubled through an anchor reaches HALF its length. Every station below stored a rope's
capacity where a distance belongs. null is the correct replacement where no source publishes a
figure - halving would swap one fabricated number for another. The single exception is
wa_south_face_5 station 7, where a source gives 'about 100 ft'.
Generated by scripts/oneoff/build-rappel-length-corrections.mjs so that `from` and `expect` are
read from the live rows rather than copied from a report.

wa_ingalls_peak_south_ridge._why: Station 2 stores 55 m on a rappel its own text brackets at 34.5-35 m ('a 60 m comes up about 5 m short ... a 70 m only just makes it'). Going in as null rather than 35: deriving 35 from 'a 70 only just makes it' is the rope-capacity arithmetic this sweep exists to remove. The bracket is recorded in the count note instead.

set.rappel_count_note: The counts on this page assume different rope setups and are all correct. On two 60 m ropes it is three rappels: a double-rope rappel from the three-bolt summit anchor to the large ledge above pitch 2, then a short one to the top of pitch 1, then one more to the base ledges. On a single 60 m rope it is four, because a 60 m falls roughly 15 ft short of the pitch-2 ledge from the pitch-3 station. Two 70 m ropes reach mid-pitch-2 from the summit and allow a scramble to the top-of-pitch-1 anchor, dropping a rappel again. Whichever setup you carry, the strong recommendation from parties who have done it is to break the descent at the pitch-3 ledge rather than running one long rappel from the summit: a crack just under the summit bolts, and a second near the slung boulder at the end of pitch 2, are both documented rope-eaters. Reported rope behaviour brackets the second rappel at roughly 35 m — a 60 m rope comes up about 5 m short of the ledge and a 70 m only just reaches — but no source states the distance, so it is recorded as unknown.

wa_liberty_bell_nw_face._why: Stations 2 and 3 look transposed. Station 2 says 'a 60m rope reaches' (so <=30 m) while storing 55; station 3 calls itself a double-rope rappel to the notch while storing 30. The same notch rappel is stored as 55 m on wa_liberty_bell_east_face.

wa_mount_rainier_kautz_glacier._why: The count note says the table is a middle count 'for a party on a single 60m rope', which cannot reach the 45 m stored at stations 1 and 2. NPS publishes only '1-3 rappels' over '300+ ft', so 45 is 300 ft halved.

An alternate option reverses the South Ridge itself via numerous short single-rope rappels off slings instead.
